entries.title: II Kings 5:1
segments: No honors or successes can secure men from trouble; and for the blessings they obtain by their own efforts, or those of others, they are indebted to God.

entries.title: II Kings 5:3
segments:
The prophet; Elisha. 
 
Servants may be the means of great blessings to their masters; and the good influence even of a pious child may be felt through a nation, and to distant countries and times.

entries.title: II Kings 5:4
segments: His lord; Ben-hadad the king of Syria.

entries.title: II Kings 5:5
segments:
He; Naaman. 
 
  Pieces; that is, shekels.  A talent of silver contained three thousand shekels.  A shekel of silver has been estimated at from fifty to sixty cents.  A shekel of gold was many times greater.  See note to

entries.title: II Kings 5:6
segments:
That thou mayest recover him; he expected the cure to be performed by Elisha, but supposed that the prophets of Israel, like those of the heathen nations, were under the direction of their monarch, and would act at his bidding. 
 
Despotic rulers often feel and act as if ministers of God in the discharge of their duties were to be subject to their control.

entries.title: II Kings 5:10
segments: Ministers who understand and do their duty, will not be elated nor overawed by the presence of the rich and great; but will make known to them with plainness and fidelity the will of God, whether they will hear or forbear.

entries.title: II Kings 5:13
segments: Servants are sometimes wiser and better than their masters, and give them advice which it would be well for them to follow.

entries.title: II Kings 5:14
segments: Simply following the diretions of God, however plain and easy, is more efficacious than the most skilful, laborious, and costly schemes of men.  These tend to feed and strengthen human pride; the other to exalt and glorify God.

entries.title: II Kings 5:15
segments: A blessing; a gift or present.

entries.title: II Kings 5:16
segments: Disinterested kindness, and doing good without expecting or wishing any earthly reward, is adapted to convey to men a correct impression of true religion.

entries.title: II Kings 5:17
segments: Two mules' burden of earth; with this it is supposed he intended to build an altar or mound, on which to offer sacrifices to Jehovah, considering the earth of Israel more sacred than that of his own country.

entries.title: II Kings 5:18
segments:
Rimmon; an idol god. 
 
  When I bow down myself; it has been supposed that he meant not as himself worshipping the idol, but only in attending on, and performing a civil duty to the king.

entries.title: II Kings 5:20
segments: The unprincipled, selfish, and covetous think it wise to take any course in which, without danger, they can get money.

entries.title: II Kings 5:22
segments: My master hath sent me; this was false.

entries.title: II Kings 5:25
segments:
Went no whither; another falsehood. 
 
Men who will sacrifice conscience for money, will tell lies in order to keep it; but the getting or keeping of money by lying, instead of being in the end a source of profit, will occasion most dreadful loss.

entries.title: II Kings 5:26
segments: Went not my heart; did I not perceive.

entries.title: II Kings 5:27
segments: For ever; as long as they should live.
